# Cave of Wonders dialogue: 20-50 minute replies - 2026-10-04

**Skill:** Ecgberht (the Cave of Wonders conversation, persona Aladdin), diagnosed from outside by the Claude Code session at John's request ("check why the dialogue in the Cave of Wonders seems to be taking so long... journal about this and figure out a fix").
**Input:** `C:\dev\Campaign\Cave of Wonders\.ecgberht\conversation-log.json` and `status-summary.json`; the Codex thread `~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/03/rollout-2026-10-03T07-22-59-01a101ee-a39b-72f2-9002-02041c8b3d8a.jsonl` (40 MB, 24 turns since 2026-10-03 07:22); Anchor `settings.json` and `model_policy.py`.
**Work:** Measured reply latency in the log and each Codex turn's length, tool calls, context size and compactions; split the longest turns into model time, tool time and compaction.
**Output:** John's messages waited 37, 39 and 20 minutes for a reply today (14:37Z, 15:30Z, 18:54Z); his 20:45Z, 20:54Z and 21:34Z messages queued behind one turn ("steward mid-turn since 14:45 (50 min) · 2 queued"). Every turn ran `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort `ultra` (settings `model_policy` = latest_supported / highest_supported, which `model_policy.validate_policy` requires). Working turns took 25-51 minutes with 14-69 tool calls each; context 176k-230k input tokens per step, and compaction ran in 7 of the last 9 turns.
**Result:** The time is the model, not the tools. In the 51-minute turn (20:51Z, 56 calls) the model took 49.5 minutes and tool runs 1.5; in the 28-minute turn (14:37Z) 27.7 vs 0.5. Each step is about one minute of ultra-effort reasoning over about 200k tokens. Three causes, in order of weight: (1) the steward does Anchor code work itself, step by step, inside the conversation turn, so the conversation is occupied for the whole job; (2) every step runs at the highest effort; (3) the one-conversation rule (W5, 2026-10-01) resumes one ever-growing thread, so each step re-reads about 200k tokens and most turns compact. Messages sent mid-turn queue silently until the turn ends.
**Friction:** The usage ledger has no rows for these bridge turns (searched the newest 40 files for the Cave folder), so durations had to be read from the Codex thread. `status-summary` showed "Tests/Journal/ETA unavailable" throughout the long turns, so John could not tell work from a hang.
**Next:** Proposed fix, for John's word (the effort rule is his): (a) the steward hands code work to a commissioned coder job and stays free to answer, saying "on it; the coder is running X" within a minute; (b) the conversation's own turns run one effort step down (`high`) while commissioned build work keeps `highest_supported`; (c) a message sent mid-turn gets an immediate receipt naming what the steward is doing and its start time; (d) the Cave thread rolls over to a fresh Codex thread when context passes about 150k, seeded from the conversation log, invisible on the page (the log, not the thread, is the conversation he sees). Recommendation: (a) and (c) first, since they keep his dialogue responsive without lowering quality on real work. Goes through an Ecgberht improvement cycle, not an ad-hoc patch. Host Claude Code (Opus 5.5), read-only diagnosis, cross_model false.
